Author: @SomaCruz500
Content:
Random MGS facts in… 3, 2… 1:


The specific Metal Gear designs that were leaked by Ocelot at the end of Metal Gear Solid were the Army’s Metal Gear Rex designs. 

Metal Gear Rex itself is a weapon that needs armor, air, naval and infantry support, even with the ability to launch invisible strikes using its railgun from practically anywhere its legs can take it. The legs making Rex the technical starting missing link between Armor and infantry that Alexander Leonovitch Granin was drunkly going on about in Snake Eater. The Marine’s Ray project was designed to act as a multipurpose fast attack weapon that was meant to capitalize on the Army’s Rex designs shortcomings and need for defenses. 

Vamp is also not actually a Vampire, Guns of the Patriots establishes this in cement (after the fight in the Rex Hangar), the “Vamp” story (meme) about being pierced to a cross and surviving on his family’s blood is a story Snake had overheard. Pretty sure Snake himself in a codec call also goes “they call him Vamp cause he’s bisexual”. Which isn’t wrong given lore. But even Snake isn’t 100% sure why his codename is Vamp. It just is and the dude leans into so well. 

All I know is Big Boss would’ve heard that Codename and *noped* right out of the mission if his conversation with Paramedic in the prison cell in Snake Eater is any indication. 

Kojima also left the threads of the Grand Scheme in the game, the Nuke was a purified Hydrogen Bomb that was going to be launched and detonated over New York City to take out the Stock exchange. There’s an entire sequence showing Arsenal Gear literally moving the Statue of Liberty before crashing into half of Manhattan (the Twin Towers were prominently shown, but apparently not overtly damaged), destroying the Stock Exchange as well, that was perhaps the biggest cut that we’ve known about.

i don't know much japanese but muta is right about how there is no "L" im japanese, but thats also sorta not true, theres also really no "R" they are mixed actually, so more like "LRA" it's not outside of the language it would just be equal to saying the "R" set of mora, but in the context of the game its meant to be white noise, or equal to static, if the patriots don't want you to know or hear the name patriots then you hear "la-le-lu-li-lo" or basically gibberish. this is further confirmed in 4 when your first talking to the weapons guy and snake says the patriots and he comes back with "la le lu li lo?" and snake just says "nevermind" knowing the guys nanomachines wont let him hear it, so he isnt being directly controlled by them (at least as far as he knows) when the dude says the la le lu li lo sent him what he really says and what he hears is "i was sent in by the patriots" cause obviously he would know their name, the nanomachines are what make this possible thats another reason snake makes sucha big deal about raiden having them and then the president knowing he has them when he heard la le lu li lo instead of patriots. another small thing about japanese, i know alot of people are like "god why do they always repeat stuff back when someone is talking?! its so annoying!" in japanese thats considered polite and shows that you are listening and paying attention to what is being told to you.

when emma says that there was a big experiment planned to give GW a bunch of complex data to analyze, shes correct, mostly, the test is currently happening, the data from the whole big shell incident was going to be the super complex data that GW would be tested with. as stated towards the end the virus isnt actually a virus to stop GW, GW''s AI is still talking to raiden at the end of the game as the colonel and rose, the whole gibberish and nonses thing could just be where the AI is updating or it could be part of the test to see how raiden performs without clear instructions from command. but thats not the patriots since they are men and not immortal, its the AI still, in metal gear solid 4 the big ship you goto at the end is arsenal gear, GW isnt the only AI made by the patriots either, but GW is still fully operational until the ending of 4 when liquid destroys it and the other AI finally completing big boss and his mission, snake eater gives alot more backstory into how big boss became big boss, but i think alot of people miss that at the end when he figures out that he was basically lied to the entire mission it makes him sad about his mentor and everything so he decides instead to destroy the patriots, seeing it more as his mentor the boss was also lied to about her role in the mission and what the goal was. 

the inside areas of arsenal are meant to be named after organs, also at one point the colonel says a bunch of japanese words, he is listing a bunch of subway stations in tokyo. the colonel is just GW's AI btw, so is rose. and i'm pretty sure the whole 20 ray fight is just a VR thing that the AI is making raiden experience through the nanomachines. or maybe it was solidus, hard to say but honestly that whole bit seems so surreal and the fact they talk about how its hard to tell the difference between reality and a game anymore right before, and there being what seems like no logical entrance to the area, then pretty much right after you wake up on the deck of the ship.

Author: @christopherescobar10
Content:
Great video! MGS2 has the best story in video games in my opinion. Its my favorite Metal Gear game too. When it released, I had not played MGS1 so I didn't end up hating Raiden like a lot of people did. In fact, I love MGS2 Raiden... more than Ninja Raiden (still a bad ass though).

It wasn't until my adult life that I became aware of how great the story of MGS2 was. Super Bunnyhop's video definitely helped with that.

With how MGS2 predicted the future, it makes it even better than ever. The plot written in 2001 (actually sooner than that; just going by release date here) is more relevant than ever. The Internet has changed so much throughout the years. 

Most MGS fans prefer MGS3 and that's fine. I love MGS3 too. But in terms of story, it peaked with MGS2. Everything went downhill with MGS4. I havent played the latter since I beat it back in 2008 or whenever it came out though. Many things I didn't like about the story in MGS4.

Anyways, I hope MGS Delta (MGS3 remake) sells well so we can get a remake of both MGS1 and 2. As long as the stories are basically the same, I'll be happy.

Oh and last thing. Like many games made back in the day with hardware limitations, if i remember correctly, the mirrors in the plant chapter bathrooms (near the location you meet Stillman) are fake. Real-time reflections take up a ton of resources so they used little tricks to make it look like a mirror reflection such as an exact copy of the bathroom flipped  and a duplicate Raiden copying everything you do. Very clever.

Author: @arctorusmedia
Content: Digital information DOES deteriorate. Each time something is copied, it runs the risk of some of its information being corrupted. Not only that, but the drives containing the information don't last forever and people have to be around to make new servers and back that data up. That is not something that might always be around. If we stop trying to preserve data, it will disappear forever. The term 'lost media' isn't fictitious.

Author: @chronosauce
Content:
As a longtime viewer (from the early days of Deep Web Browsing), I could not possibly be happier about this pivot in content. I've always valued your research and insight on topics like cyber security, the gaming industry, and Internet horror, and this video managed to intersect with some of your most apparent strengths as a creator. I can tell a lot of effort went into this video.

As a fan, and as a fellow human who has also been online since the late nineties, I don't hold it against you that you got swept up in the slop machine that's taking over Youtube and other platforms. If anything, given your well established expertise in the Internet, I think it goes to show how any of us can get caught up in this cycle, and you shining a spotlight on your own journey away from that bubble was the prompt that I needed to re-examine what sort of content I'm consuming online.

I'm glad to see you back to this sort of content, and I'm excited to see what you'll do next. Welcome back to the platform!

Author: @SirOregano
Content:
It's a shame that there are too many people who haven't even played MGS2, or even understand the messages the game conveys. Being able to think for yourself, finding what to believe in and what to pass on are our rights as individuals, but many people become easily swayed and lose sight of the bigger picture. "Find the meaning behind the words, then decide." imo, is one of the most important things to get ingrained into your head as far as communicating with other humans goes. This goes without saying that there is a double edged balance you must maintain when it comes to "free will". Don't become easily impressionable and take everything you hear or see as empirical fact, but also don't obsess over the many possible ulterior motives/messages/conspiracies that may make you end up falling too deep into a rabbit hole. It is hard to be 100% "self aware" all the time. We all slip up and regurgitate nonsense from time to time. To quote Max Derrat's video "The Most Profound Moment in Gaming History" (Highly recommend you watch it if you haven't) "This is why people separate into political echo chambers and will only surround themselves with people who confirm their political biases as to avoid facing "truth" or opposing arguments." Some people are too far gone when it comes to ideals/faith and the most we can do is learn to recognize it, and take what is propagated by said individual, with a grain of salt. Still hear people out when any debate over any subject is made, political or not. But really pay attention and listen to how they came to their conclusion. If that person is able to handle the emotional weight of being objectively incorrect and is able to face truth head on, then that person is one worth keeping around. I'm currently saving up to get the NTSC cover art of the game tattooed on my shoulder as a reminder on how to live, because we all make the mistake of letting emotion get in the way of things. Nobody likes to hear that they are wrong about something, especially after dedicating the finite time of their life towards it. To be human is to have flaws, and the first step towards improvement is recognizing those flaws, taking it on the chin and owning it. Only then after introspection, can you actually develop your sense of "self" and define who YOU are. This game and the meaning behind the words that I take from it have helped mold me into who I am today, while far from the version of myself I'd like to end up as, it has greatly helped me find out who I am and who I would like to be. (Ironic because its technically not my own idea, it was something Snake told me :P ) 

Amazing video as always Muta, thank you for the time you have put into this. And thank you Hideo Kojima for making Metal Gear Solid 2
